data.gender_notes: Addam is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Addam is derived from the name Adam, meaning 'man' or 'earth'. In the Old Testament, Addam is the name of the eldest son of Shem and the ancestor of many biblical figures. The name Addam carries the meaning “Son of Adam” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Addam usually hope their child will grow to embody son of adam and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name rooted in the creation story, symbolizing the connection between humanity and the earth.
data.etymology: Addam belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of Adam.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Addam total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: אדמ
in_hebrew.meaning: אדם נוצרי, בן אדמה, אדמת אלוהים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אדמ מקורו בשפה העברית ומשמעותו בן אדמה, אדם, או אדמת אלוהים. הוא קשור קשר הדוק לאדם הראשון שנברא על ידי אלוהים, לפי ספר בראשית. השם נושא משמעות רבה בתרבות היהודית והנוצרית כאחד, ומסמל את הקשר בין האדם לאלוהים.

in_greek.name: Άδδαμ
in_greek.meaning: Άνθρωπος του Θεού, Γη του Θεού
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Άδδαμ προέρχεται από την Εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει άνθρωπος του Θεού ή γη του Θεού. Στο Χριστιανισμό, το όνομα συνδέεται με τον πρώτο άνθρωπο που δημιουργήθηκε από τον Θεό, όπως αναφέρεται στο Βιβλίο της Γένεσης. Το όνομα έχει μεγάλη σημασία τόσο στην Εβραϊκή όσο και στην Χριστιανική παράδοση.

in_latin.name: Adam
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Adam originem in lingua Hebraea habet et significat hominem Dei vel terram Dei. In traditione Christiana, nomen Adam refertur ad primum hominem a Deo creato, ut in libro Genesis descriptum est. Nomen hoc magnam vim et significationem habet in cultura tanto Judaica quanto Christiana.
